A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FI-NRL, GVT and RGVT research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the changed title, formatting and appendix numbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original node-classification experiments, component ablations, runtime measurements, and additional experiments with non-attributed graphs and LLM-embedded features.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original RGVT results with TabPFN, recurrent-depth and representation analyses, and evaluations under additional comparison pipelines. Some comparator scores are explicitly adopted from prior work.

M1.justification: The GVT encoder, recurrent architecture and training objective remain unchanged. Appendix L adds RGVT+TabPFN as an optional predictor variant, replacing per-dataset classifier fitting with in-context prediction. This is a limited extension of the inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same 28 main benchmark graphs, six non-attributed graph settings and seven graphs with LLM-embedded features. V2's new 17- and 23-dataset comparisons use subsets of existing coverage; they introduce no additional graph domains or prediction tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds comparisons with NodeFormer, LSGNN, DirGNN and SGFormer in Table 14, and TS-Net variants, TAG and NodePFN in Tables 16–17. Those tables also introduce the Products-pretrained GraphAny variant. The original comparisons remain, substantially expanding the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The original experimental settings are retained, but v2 adds separate RGVT evaluations under TAG and NodePFN pipelines, a TabPFN comparison restricted to 17 compatible datasets, and transfer-depth sweeps. Figure 9 also introduces Elo and improvability metrics. These expand the evaluation design without establishing changes to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: New appendices analyze predictor substitution, transfer-depth sensitivity across 28 graphs, and t-SNE representations on Amazon Photo and Coauthor CS. The transfer-depth analysis differs from the retained pretraining-depth ablation. The aggregation heatmaps also replace the first-versus-eighth-layer comparison with a comparison between random-walk and symmetric-normalized views.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent runs with means and standard deviations and retain the identical Wilcoxon signed-rank analysis in Appendix A. Additional result tables and plots do not establish a changed repetition count, uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: The original table means and standard deviations are unchanged, but substantial results are added. Table 13 reports 70.70% for RGVT+TabPFN versus 70.03% for RGVT+MLP on 17 datasets; Table 14 reports 71.00% for SGFormer versus 71.13% for RGVT+MLP. Tables 16–17 add pipeline-specific comparisons with newer GFMs, rather than same-setting improvements over v1. V2 also introduces a 5 ms inference statement that conflicts with the retained 0.052 seconds in Table 10.

T1.justification: The formal view-space definitions, permutation-equivariance statements, linear-aggregation analysis, local-linearization result and proofs in Appendices B–E are substantively retained. Notation, equation numbering and explanatory wording change without adding or revising formal results.

C1.justification: Despite the new title and revised framing, the abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: FI-NRL, view space, GVT and RGVT. The headline claims of +8.93% over GraphAny and at least +3.30% over 12 individually tuned GNNs also remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 9 substantially expands the discussion of absent explicit cross-feature mixing, its scalability tradeoff, predictor-training requirements, TabPFN limitations and recurrent-depth selection overhead. New analyses support interpretations about preserving feature structure and using fixed depths. Appendix O acknowledges narrower accuracy margins against newer GNNs and emphasizes adaptation efficiency.

D1.justification: V2 newly supplies a code-and-checkpoint link in the abstract and reports approximately three days on four H200 GPUs for the additional GNN comparisons. Existing hyperparameters, optimizer, stopping rules and A6000 runtime setup remain unchanged. The added pipelines receive limited implementation detail.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantive positioning relative to tabular foundation models and recent fully inductive graph models, particularly TAG and NodePFN. Previously cited TS-Net becomes an evaluated comparator. New discussion and citations for recent GNNs broaden the assessment of competitiveness and adaptation cost beyond the original GraphAny-centered comparison.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, contributions become an explicit numbered list, and several section headings and explanations are revised. The ablation and visualization subsections exchange order, a dedicated Discussion section is introduced, and new appendices shift the dataset-details and full-results sections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column proceedings layout. The original overview figure is split into two figures, aggregation heatmaps are redesigned, and new depth, representation and comparison plots and tables are added. Table 1 loses its relative-improvement rows, while the original full GNN table is enlarged and split across Tables 20–21.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the paper through contemporary comparator evaluations, useful transfer-depth and representation analyses, more explicit design limitations, and documented code/checkpoint access. These improve the completeness and practical interpretation of the retained findings. Limited documentation of the added pipelines and the new 5 ms versus 52 ms runtime inconsistency temper the gains, yielding a modest net improvement.
